Pointer off. Mapped system navigation and direct motion remain independent.
Pointer on. Coordinate actions follow the existing input restrictions.

Camera access recognizes your hand. Accessibility performs the actions you request. Neither permission arms actions.
Front-camera hand recognition, processed on your device.
Execute device actions that you explicitly request.
Keep the phone steady and your hand in view. Start with Back, Home and Recents. Pointer calibration is optional.
On your device, by your choice.
Hand recognition runs on device. Diagnostic recording captures frame data and sampled camera images locally. Nothing is sent automatically; review files before saving or sharing them.
Form the pose deliberately, then return to a neutral hand before the next command. This guide does not score recognition or send device actions.
A deliberate move. A clear direction.
Use the pose assigned to Arm motion. Ordinary hand travel does not issue commands.
Establish a comfortable starting position after the entry pose.
Up/down scrolls. Left/right swipes. Each movement is one command; use the entry pose again for the next.
Uses your hand position in the camera, not phone tilt or a gyroscope.
No gesture is assigned to Arm motion yet.
Instruction only. Device actions remain disarmed; no recognition result is simulated.
Pointer tools are optional. Use thumb-to-middle contact for clicking; pointer clicking and classifier gestures have independent switches.
Check pointer reach with actions disarmed. This is a live pointer preview, not a scored accuracy test.
Pointer reach only. Gesture navigation does not require calibration.
Device actions are disarmed for this screen. Returning to Control never arms automatically.
Record session evidence locally. Prepare a PDF summary and ZIP bundle, recover earlier recordings, then choose what to save or share.
Read-only vision and dispatch evidence. Experimental filter selection affects runtime behavior; keep ordinary controls unchanged.
Saved recordings, export recovery and sharing are available below.
Changing this diagnostic filter changes pointer output. It does not modify your gesture assignments.
Aergis translates deliberate hand poses and camera-observed hand movements into Android actions. Gesture control comes first; the pointer is an optional precision tool.
Experimental gaze remains a separate lab. It is not part of gesture control or a production input guarantee.
